title: N-Acetylcysteine (NAC)
heading: Best human evidence for cutting cannabis cravings and supporting abstinence
subheading: Normalizes glutamate–dopamine signaling. May reduce urges in other addictions and support mood regulation.
proof: [{"link":"https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0376871617302624","text":"Teens with CUD taking 1,200 mg twice daily had higher abstinence vs placebo in an RCT"},{"link":"https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/22706327/","text":"2022 review: overall signals for reduced use/craving; mechanism fits addiction biology"}]
instructions: ["🍳 Morning: 600–1,200 mg with breakfast","🌆 Evening: 600–1,200 mg (optional) if cravings hit later","🌙 Night: Not required","💨 Before usual smoke time: An extra 600 mg 30–60 min prior can blunt cue-triggered cravings"]
caution: May potentiate nitroglycerin (low blood pressure, headache); can thin blood; GI upset possible. Talk to your clinician if on anticoagulants or before surgery.

title: Cannabidiol (CBD, THC-free)
heading: Human trial evidence that oral CBD reduces cannabis use
subheading: May calm anxiety and improve sleep without a 'high'. General anxiolytic effects; may smooth mood swings.
proof: [{"link":"https://psychiatryonline.org/doi/10.1176/appi.ajp.2012.12010055","text":"Phase 2a RCT: CBD 400–800 mg/day ↓ cannabis use vs placebo over 4 weeks"},{"link":"https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2021/210365s012s013lbl.pdf","text":"CBD has meaningful drug–drug interaction and liver enzyme signals at higher doses"}]
instructions: ["🍳 Morning: 50–150 mg (optional) for daytime anxiety","🌆 Evening: 100–300 mg for wind-down","🌙 Night: 100–300 mg for sleep","💨 Before usual smoke time: 50–150 mg 60 min before triggers"]
caution: CBD inhibits CYP enzymes (e.g., CYP2C19/3A4) ↑ can raise levels of SSRIs, benzos, antiepileptics, warfarin; monitor and consult a clinician. Liver enzyme elevations reported at higher doses and with valproate.

title: Melatonin
heading: Resets sleep rhythm to counter rebound insomnia and vivid dreams
subheading: During cannabis break. May improve sleep quality; calming.
proof: [{"link":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9366042/","text":"Systematic review in substance use: mixed across drugs, but sleep and mood improved in several groups"},{"link":"https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38491827/","text":"THC-withdrawn mice: melatonin reduced withdrawal-like behaviors; mechanistic support"}]
instructions: ["🌙 Night: 1–3 mg 30–60 min before bed; use nightly for 1–2 weeks, then taper off"]
caution: Avoid combining with sedatives; fluvoxamine (CYP1A2 inhibitor) can boost melatonin levels ~12–17×—avoid that combo. May cause next-day drowsiness or vivid dreams.

title: Magnesium (glycinate preferred)
heading: Calms the nervous system, easing withdrawal-related anxiety
subheading: NMDA blockade helps sleep. Stress resilience; may cut withdrawal severity (shown in opioids).
proof: [{"link":"https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/12887140/","text":"RCT: magnesium improved sleep in primary insomnia"},{"link":"https://www.jsatjournal.com/article/S2949-8759%2824%2900019-5/abstract","text":"Double-blind clinical trial: IV magnesium reduced opioid withdrawal severity"}]
instructions: ["🌆 Evening: 200–300 mg (common) with a snack","🌙 Night: If sensitive, split dose and take bulk at night","💨 Before usual smoke time: 100–200 mg if evening anxiety is a trigger"]
caution: Kidney disease—avoid high doses (accumulation). Can cause loose stools (citrate > glycinate). May enhance effects of other BP-lowering or CNS-depressant meds.

title: Omega-3 (Fish Oil; high EPA)
heading: Supports mood and endocannabinoid balance
subheading: Early trials show reduced cravings in smokers (addiction-relevant). Brain and heart health; anti-inflammatory.
proof: [{"link":"https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/0269881114536477","text":"RCTs: omega-3 reduced cigarette craving and consumption vs placebo"},{"link":"https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21278728/","text":"Endocannabinoid link: omega-3 deficiency impairs CB1-mediated synaptic function"}]
instructions: ["🍳 Morning: 1,000–2,000 mg EPA+DHA with food","🌆 Evening/Night: Split dose if needed","💨 Before usual smoke time: Take with the prior meal for steadier levels"]
caution: High doses can increase bleeding risk (warfarin/anticoagulants) and should be stopped before surgery; take with meals to reduce GI upset.

title: L-Theanine
heading: Promotes 'calm focus' to smooth anxiety/irritability without sedation
proof: [{"link":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6836118/","text":"4-week RCT: 200 mg/day improved anxiety, sleep quality, and executive function in stressed adults"},{"link":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8475422/","text":"Placebo-controlled data show physiological relaxation (↑ alpha waves) and reduced state anxiety"},{"link":"https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21208586/","text":"Clinical adjunct trials suggest anxiolytic effects in severe anxiety spectra"}]
instructions: ["🍳 Morning: 100–200 mg; pair with coffee if you use caffeine","🌆 Evening: 100–200 mg if anxious","🌙 Night: 100–200 mg for pre-sleep calm (non-sedating)","💨 Before usual smoke time: 100–200 mg 30–60 min before known triggers"]
caution: Generally well-tolerated; may mildly lower blood pressure and can enhance sedatives.

title: Passionflower (Passiflora incarnata)
heading: Herbal anxiolytic; animal data show it blocks THC-withdrawal signs
subheading: Human data show less anxiety during opioid detox. Sleep quality, pre-op anxiety.
proof: [{"link":"https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/31527485/","text":"THC-dependent mice: benzoflavone from passionflower prevented withdrawal"},{"link":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6770181/","text":"Opioid withdrawal RCT: added passionflower ↓ anxiety/mental symptoms vs clonidine alone"}]
instructions: ["🌆 Evening: 250–500 mg standardized extract","🌙 Night: 250–500 mg 30–60 min before bed","💨 Before usual smoke time: 250 mg if evening anxiety is a trigger"]
caution: Additive sedation with alcohol/benzos; avoid in pregnancy.

title: Citicoline (CDP-choline)
heading: Cognitive support; improves attention/executive function in cannabis users
subheading: 500 mg/day for 8 weeks showed improvement. Supports membrane repair and dopamine signaling.
proof: [{"link":"https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanpsy/article/PIIS2215-0366%2820%2930290-X/abstract","text":"RCT in adult cannabis users showed attention/task performance gains on citicoline vs placebo"}]
instructions: ["🍳 Morning: 250–500 mg with food","🌆 Evening: 250 mg (optional) if splitting","🌙 Night: Avoid (can be alerting)","💨 Before usual smoke time: 250 mg if you reach for cannabis out of low focus"]
caution: Usually well-tolerated; rare insomnia, headache, or GI upset. Use caution with bipolar disorder (any activating agent could aggravate mania).

title: L-Tyrosine
heading: Dopamine precursor that maintains alertness under stress/sleep loss
subheading: Supportive (not a craving treatment). Supports working memory in cold/overnight stress.
proof: [{"link":"https://uknowledge.uky.edu/behavsci_facpub/37/","text":"Under sleep deprivation and stress, tyrosine restored cognitive performance acutely in controlled studies"}]
instructions: ["🍳 Morning: 500 mg on an empty stomach","🌆 Evening/Night: Avoid if it makes you wired","💨 Before usual smoke time: 500 mg if you typically smoke to push through fatigue"]
caution: Avoid with hyperthyroidism; use caution in bipolar disorder (may trigger agitation); don't stack with stimulants without medical guidance.

title: Vitamin-B Complex
heading: Addresses fatigue and cognition by correcting possible B-vitamin shortfalls
subheading: RCTs show reduced work stress and improved mood in healthy adults. Supports nerve health; B12 deficiency causes fatigue and cognitive issues.
proof: [{"link":"https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/21905094/","text":"90-day RCTs: high-dose B complex reduced perceived stress and improved mood in working adults"},{"link":"https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/VitaminB12-HealthProfessional/","text":"B12 deficiency is linked to fatigue and cognitive symptoms; correcting deficiency improves energy"}]
instructions: ["🍳 Morning: Standard B-complex or B-100 with food","🌆 Evening/Night: Avoid (can be alerting)","💨 Before usual smoke time: If energy slumps trigger use, ensure you've taken your morning dose"]
caution: Generally safe; very high B6 for long periods can cause neuropathy—use labeled doses.

title: Ginger (Zingiber officinale)
heading: Natural antiemetic; useful for withdrawal-related nausea
subheading: Reasonable for withdrawal-related nausea. May also help mild dyspepsia.
proof: [{"link":"https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4755634/","text":"Multiple RCTs/meta-analyses support ginger for nausea (pregnancy, post-op, and some chemo settings)"},{"link":"https://www.nccih.nih.gov/health/ginger","text":"NCCIH notes evidence for nausea/vomiting (esp. pregnancy)"}]
instructions: ["🍳 Morning: 250–500 mg standardized extract with food","💨 Before usual nausea window/smoke time: 250–500 mg 30–60 min prior","🌆 Evening/Night: 250 mg if symptoms recur"]
caution: May worsen heartburn/reflux in some; caution with anticoagulants at high supplemental doses.
